## Goal
- Execute Step 3 Batch 1 only: reconcile at most five highest-priority IVX IA Chat/autonomous-routing files into the owner-controlled baseline, test, document, commit, and push without deployment.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Select no more than five files, limited to IVX IA Chat intent routing, engineering capability responses, conversation context, tool selection, and autonomous worker state/completion.
- Exclude iOS assets, Maestro, APK configuration, CI workflows, unrelated backend services, generated files, and obsolete files.
- Preserve owner GitHub production fixes, tested workspace engineering-intent fixes, and zero Rork runtime dependencies.
- Do surgical/manual merges; do not replace a full file unless necessary.
- Add/update focused regression tests and run relevant tests after each file.
- Run TypeScript for affected packages; stop on any regression.
- Required English and Spanish coverage:
  - “Can you create an app from scratch?”
  - “Can you create a new module?”
  - “Fix owner login.”
  - “Deploy this change.”
  - “How many active properties?”
- Required behavior:
  - Engineering questions select engineering intents.
  - Property questions select business-data intent.
  - Engineering questions must not query `jv_deals` or property tables.
  - Direct yes/no capability questions receive direct, honest answers.
- Create:
  - `audit/reconciliation-batch-1.md`
  - `audit/reconciliation-batch-1-tests.json`
- Commit only after all Batch 1 tests pass, using:
  - `fix(ivx-ai): reconcile engineering intent and autonomous routing`
- Push after committing; do not deploy or begin Batch 2.

## Progress
### Done
- Step 1 completed with 62 candidate inventory; source lineage and production baseline established.
- Step 2 reconciliation planning completed:
  - `audit/reconciliation-matrix.json`
  - `audit/reconciliation-matrix.md`
  - `audit/reconciliation-summary.md`
- Step 2 matrix action totals:
  - `KEEP_GITHUB`: 4
  - `KEEP_WORKSPACE`: 2
  - `MERGE_MANUALLY`: 25
  - `IGNORE_GENERATED`: 5
  - `ARCHIVE_OBSOLETE`: 19
  - `BLOCK_SECRET`: 0
  - `NEEDS_OWNER_DECISION`: 7
- Confirmed owner GitHub and production baseline:
  - `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
- Confirmed clean owner clone `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit` is at:
  - `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
- Began Batch 1 read-only candidate research.
- Read `.rork/skills/platforms/SKILL.md`; no app creation action is relevant.
- Compared six preliminary candidates against `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit`:
  - `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx` has the only substantive workspace-vs-owner functional change.
  - `backend/api/ivx-autonomy.ts` differs only in a comment: `RORK_AUTO_SYNC_ENABLED` → `IVX_AUTO_SYNC_ENABLED`.
  - `backend/api/ivx-autonomous-runs.ts`, `backend/api/ivx-autonomous-task-engine-api.ts`, `backend/api/ivx-scoped-memory.ts`, and `backend/services/ivx-scoped-memory-store.ts` are reported as non-functional formatting/comment-only differences in the research result.
- Located relevant existing coverage:
  - `expo/__tests__/ivx-send-trigger-policy.test.ts`
  - `expo/__tests__/ivx-owner-ai-orchestrator.test.ts`
  - `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.test.ts`
  - `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-developer-narrative.regression.test.ts`
  - `backend/services/ivx-unified-ai-gate-pipeline.test.ts`
  - `backend/__tests__/ivx-scoped-memory-store.test.ts`
- No Batch 1 source change, test execution, TypeScript execution, commit, push, or deployment has occurred yet.

### In Progress
- Select the final Batch 1 set of no more than five files based on functional relevance, rather than merging formatting-only differences.
- Inspect owner intent-routing, conversation-state, tool-selection, and autonomous-completion behavior against required English/Spanish prompts.
- Determine whether focused regression additions belong in existing tests or require new test files.

### Blocked
- Workspace Git object database does not contain owner baseline `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`; direct local commands failed:
  - `fatal: bad object d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
- Owner baseline comparison must use `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit`.
- Existing Batch 1 candidate set from the Step 2 same-path delta has only one demonstrated functional workspace change (`expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`); the required engineering-intent behavior appears primarily in files not listed as manual-diff candidates and needs careful scope interpretation before edits.
- Local `origin` remains Rork-managed, not confirmed owner GitHub:
  - `https://git:e2b-egress-managed@rork-git-router.rork-direct.workers.dev/git/j2l8t44588ix9ns7b57mu`
- Owner-GitHub push authentication/remote is not yet confirmed for the required final push.

## Key Decisions
- Treat owner GitHub `main` / production SHA `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7` as the owner-controlled baseline.
- Do not merge a file merely because it appears in the Step 2 `MERGE_MANUALLY` group; Batch 1 selection must be driven by functional routing/state relevance.
- `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx` remains the leading Batch 1 merge candidate:
  - workspace imports `shouldStartAssistantBeforePersistence`
  - local-first `send_and_ai` / `ai_only` invokes the assistant before send-queue persistence resolves
  - send-only, attachment, and remote-first behavior remains persistence-first
  - intent classification itself is not changed by this UI repair.
- Preserve direct, evidence-qualified answers for capability questions; do not claim autonomous completion based solely on job attachment or narrative output.
- Do not deploy during Batch 1.

## Next Steps
- 1. Inspect exact owner/workspace diffs for `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx` using `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit`, identify the surgical hunk, and select remaining scoped files only if they have real behavior to reconcile.
- 2. Inspect `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.ts` and its callers for engineering/business-data/tool-routing behavior for all required English/Spanish prompts.
- 3. Add focused tests asserting engineering intent, business-data intent, no property-table access for engineering prompts, and honest direct capability answers.
- 4. Apply each selected file merge one at a time and run its focused tests immediately.
- 5. Run TypeScript checks for affected backend and Expo packages.
- 6. Create `audit/reconciliation-batch-1.md` and `audit/reconciliation-batch-1-tests.json` with exact merge/test evidence.
- 7. If all checks pass, commit with `fix(ivx-ai): reconcile engineering intent and autonomous routing`.
- 8. Verify the owner GitHub push target, push, record local/remote SHAs, then stop without deployment or Batch 2.

## Critical Context
- Current workspace command reported:
  - branch: `main`
  - HEAD: `22721cd3d54773c480fd730f7fc8cc9f9d69a609`
- Earlier Step 1 workspace audit HEAD was:
  - `64e2433171169a00c32922ba08a65e5c2f9bc278`
- Owner/production baseline:
  - owner repository: `ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform`
  - owner branch: `main`
  - SHA: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
  - production health URL: `https://api.ivxholding.com/health`
- `expo/src/modules/chat/services/ivxSendTriggerPolicy.ts`:
  - workspace-only tested policy.
  - returns true only for `localFirstChatMode` and mode `send_and_ai` or `ai_only`.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-conversation-state.ts` documents the state-loss scenario:
  - owner asks “How many properties do we have?”
  - approval follow-up must retain original business-data intent instead of becoming a generic deployment plan.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-conversation-state.ts` currently treats:
  - code/deployment verbs as `code_change` or `deployment`
  - broad status terms cautiously to avoid capturing engineering questions.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.ts` has existing app-build/developer-execution routing and deployment signals; it must be verified for required Spanish equivalents.
- `backend/services/ivx-unified-ai-gate-pipeline.test.ts` already contains owner-login protection coverage, including `fix owner login`.
- A malformed comparison command used shell syntax unsupported by `sh` and failed with:
  - `sh: 1: Bad substitution`
- Another multi-file `git diff --no-index` invocation failed because it accepts only two paths:
  - `usage: git diff --no-index [<options>] <path> <path>`

## Relevant Files
- `audit/reconciliation-matrix.json`: authoritative Step 2 recommendations and Batch 1 candidate context.
- `audit/reconciliation-matrix.md`: human-readable Step 2 reconciliation matrix.
- `audit/reconciliation-summary.md`: Step 2 action totals, risk list, and approved execution order.
- `audit/reconciliation-batch-1.md`: required Batch 1 merge-decision/test report; not yet created.
- `audit/reconciliation-batch-1-tests.json`: required machine-readable Batch 1 test evidence; not yet created.
- `/tmp/ivx-owner-audit`: clean owner baseline clone at `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`.
- `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`: only inspected Batch 1 candidate with demonstrated functional workspace behavior; local-first assistant start must be merged surgically.
- `expo/src/modules/chat/services/ivxSendTriggerPolicy.ts`: workspace-only local-first policy retained by Step 2; supports Batch 1 chat behavior.
- `expo/__tests__/ivx-send-trigger-policy.test.ts`: current focused local-first send policy regression coverage.
- `expo/__tests__/ivx-owner-ai-orchestrator.test.ts`: existing chat orchestration/routing-state coverage.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.ts`: likely primary location for engineering intent, app/module capability, deployment, and tool-routing assertions.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-intent-router.test.ts`: existing planner/intent routing coverage; likely test extension target.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-developer-narrative.regression.test.ts`: regression coverage for developer narrative/execution intent.
- `backend/services/ivx-unified-ai-gate-pipeline.ts`: owner/session execution guard behavior.
- `backend/services/ivx-unified-ai-gate-pipeline.test.ts`: includes `fix owner login` protection tests.
- `backend/services/ivx-owner-conversation-state.ts`: durable pending-action context and business-data follow-up handling.
- `backend/__tests__/ivx-scoped-memory-store.test.ts`: scoped-memory isolation/context tests.
- `backend/services/ivx-scoped-memory-store.ts`: Step 2 high-risk context storage candidate; current difference is reportedly only terminal newline.
- `backend/api/ivx-scoped-memory.ts`: scoped-memory API candidate; current difference is reportedly non-functional.
- `backend/api/ivx-autonomous-task-engine-api.ts`: tool/agent/task-completion API candidate; current difference is reportedly non-functional.
- `backend/api/ivx-autonomous-runs.ts`: autonomous-run state API candidate; current difference is reportedly non-functional.
- `backend/api/ivx-autonomy.ts`: autonomous API candidate; only observed difference is auto-sync kill-switch comment text.

     2|name: platforms
     3|description: Use this skill whenever the user asks to create, scaffold, add, or
     4|  set up an app in the current Rork workspace, including requests like "create
     5|  an iOS app for this website" or adding a native iOS/Swift, Android/Kotlin,
     6|  Expo/React Native, or web app alongside an existing app. This unlocks the
     7|  createApp tool; do not reject app-creation requests just because another app
     8|  already exists.
     9|---
    10|
    11|### createApp
    12|
    13|Create a new app inside the workspace. Writes template files into a subfolder and
    14|creates/updates the root rork.json manifest.
    15|
    16|When to call:
    17|- Empty workspace: you MUST call this before writing any code.
    18|- Existing workspace: call when the user asks to add another app (e.g. an iOS app alongside an
    19|  existing web app).
    20|
    21|Picking `framework` for the FIRST app:
    22|- Default to the user's selected platform (named in the new-project nudge).
    23|- Override only on clear intent for another platform — by name OR by use:
    24|  iPhone/iPad/App Store/widget → `swift`; Android/Play Store → `kotlin`;
    25|  website/dashboard/"deploy to my domain"/runs in a browser → `web`. Intent need not be the
    26|  exact word ("deploy it to my domain" → `web`); the app's genre alone is not intent (a
    27|  "CS2-style FPS is a PC game" stays on the selected platform).
    28|- createApp rejects the first attempt whose `framework` differs from the selected platform.
    29|  If the user really did ask for the other platform, just call createApp again with the same
    30|  `framework` and it goes through; otherwise switch to the selected platform.
    31|- `react-native` is only valid when the project was originally started with React Native;
    32|  the call is rejected otherwise. React native is deprecated and will be removed in the future.
    33|- Swift 3D games / RealityKit games → `swift`. Decide orientation from the requested genre,
    34|  camera, and controls before creating the app.
    35|- Use `swiftTemplateProfile: "landscape-3d-game"` when the chosen orientation is landscape:
    36|  explicit landscape/horizontal requests, generic or ambiguous Swift/RealityKit 3D games,
    37|  racing/driving/flight, FPS/TPS/shooters, arena combat, action RPG/open-world/adventure,
    38|  sports/fighting, dual-stick controls, wide tactical maps, or designs that need a wide
    39|  camera view or two-thumb controls.
    40|- Do not use the landscape profile for portrait-first games: endless/lane runners, vertical
    41|  runners/climbers/fallers, one-tap or swipe hypercasual games, idle/merge/tycoon/collection
    42|  games, card/board/puzzle/gacha games, vertical shooters, rhythm lane games, regular apps,
    43|  AR/model viewers, or non-game 3D showcases.
    44|
    45|Ask the user for a clear app name/alias, then call this tool with the name and framework.
    46|If a Swift/RealityKit 3D game's orientation is ambiguous, default to landscape and include
    47|`swiftTemplateProfile`; do not stop to ask the user. Omit the profile when the user
    48|explicitly requests portrait/vertical or the prompt clearly matches a portrait-first genre.
    49|The repo folder path is derived automatically from that name, for example `ios-client-demo`,
    50|`android-field-team`, or `web-marketing-site`.
    51|
    52|Temporary rollout constraint: only one app per framework can be created right now. If the
    53|project already has an iOS, Android, or Web app, do not create another one of that same
    54|framework yet.
